dervis-irab:1-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بَنانَهُ): البنان are the fingertips; it is a plural, or a collective noun, of بنانة — two views. In al-Mukhtār: «البنانة is the singular of البنان, which are the fingertips. One says بنان مخضّب (dyed fingertips, in the masculine), because every plural between which and its singular there is nothing but the hāʾ is treated as both feminine and masculine».
(بَرِقَ): برق يبرق, of the class of دخل, برقا, بروقا, برقانا and بريقا: البرق (the lightning) appeared; the thing shone and glittered; the sky: lightning appeared from it; the man: threatened. And برِق يبرَق, of the class of تعب, برقا: he was bewildered and dazed and could not see. It has been read both ways.
(خَسَفَ): it darkened and its light went.
(وَزَرَ): a refuge in which one fortifies oneself; everything you take refuge in, whether a mountain or other, and escape by, is your وزر.

* I'rab:
(لا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ): Al-Zamakhsharī said: bringing لا before the verb of oath is widespread in their speech and their poems. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
ولا وأبيك ابنة العامريّ ... لا يدّعي القوم أني أفرّ
(No, by your father, daughter of al-ʿĀmirī, the people shall not claim that I flee.)
The entry of the negative لا before the oath was common in the tongue of the Arabs only because it is usually for rejecting and negating the opponent's claim; so the implied form is: "no, that does not happen, by the right of your father". Ghawiyya ibn Salmā said:
ألا نادت أمامة باحتمال ... لتحزنني فلا بك ما أبالي
(Lo, Umāma called out the departure, to grieve me — no, by you, I do not care.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Its benefit is the emphasis of the oath. They said it is a connective (ṣila), like that in «لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب». It was objected that it is added only in the middle of speech, not at its beginning; and they answered that the Qur'an is like a single sūra, its parts connected with one another. The objection is valid, because it has not occurred as redundant except in the middle of speech, but the answer is not sound — do you not see how Imruʾ al-Qays added it at the opening of his ode? The right view is to say it is for negation, and the meaning is that He does not swear by a thing except to magnify it; His saying, the Exalted, «فلا أقسم بمواقع النجوم، وإنه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم» shows you that. So it is as though, by bringing in the particle of negation, He says:
My magnifying it by swearing by it is as no magnifying, meaning that it deserves more than that. It has also been said that لا negates speech and rejects it before the oath, as though they denied the resurrection, and it was said: No — i.e. the matter is not as you have said — and then it was said: I swear by the Day of Resurrection». It has also been said that it is a rejection of their speech when they denied the resurrection, as though He said: the matter is not as you have said; I swear by the Day of Resurrection. This is the view of al-Farrāʾ and many grammarians. Discussion of it preceded in al-Wāqiʿa, so renew your acquaintance with it. أقسم is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), whose fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنا; بيوم القيامة is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أقسم.
(وَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالنَّفْسِ اللَّوَّامَةِ): conjoined to the previous clause; اللوامة is a naʿt (adjective) of النفس, i.e. the one that blames itself on the Day of Resurrection for whatever shortcoming it committed, or the one that never ceases to blame itself in this world. It is narrated that he, upon him be peace, said: «There is no soul, righteous or wicked, but it will blame itself on the Day of Resurrection: if it did good, it will say: Why did I not do more? And if it did evil, it will say: Would that I had refrained from evil». The answer to the oath is omitted, i.e. "you will surely be resurrected", indicated by what follows it, which is:
(أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسانُ أَلَّنْ نَجْمَعَ عِظامَهُ): the hamza is for a question of denial and rebuke; يحسب is an imperfect verb, nominative; الإنسان is the agent. أن is lightened from the heavy (أنّ); its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and لن and what lies within its scope are in the position of the khabar (predicate); the separator here is the particle of negation. The lightened أن and what lies within its scope fill the place of the two objects of يحسب. عظامه is the object of نجمع, for resurrection and bringing back to life. Al-Naḥḥās said: He singled out the bones only because they are the mould of the body.
(بَلى قادِرِينَ عَلى أَنْ نُسَوِّيَ بَنانَهُ): بلى is a particle of answer; it affirms what comes after the negation over which the question extends. قادرين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of the implied verb indicated by the particle of answer, i.e. "yes, We will gather them, being able"; this is the right view. Some said it is accusative as the khabar of a concealed كان, i.e. "yes, We were able in the beginning"; and that is not so good. قادرون was read in the nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "yes, We are able". على is a preposition; the maṣdariyya أن and what lies within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made genitive by على, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قادرين. The agent of نسوي is a latent pronoun, its implied form being نحن, and بنانه is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). According to Sībawayh, قادرين is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being نجمعها قادرين.
(بَلْ يُرِيدُ الْإِنْسانُ لِيَفْجُرَ أَمامَهُ): بل is a conjunction for transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī). يريد is conjoined to أيحسب, so it may, like it, be a question, or it may be an affirmation. بل may also be for mere transitional digression without conjunction, as though He turned away from the first speech and took up another. يريد الإنسان is an imperfect verb and its agent; the object of يريد is omitted. The meaning is: rather, man wants to remain and persist in his state of not being bound by the bond of faith, so that he may run on in his wickedness and continue in his error. The lām is for reason (taʿlīl); يفجر is an imperfect verb, accusative by أن concealed after the lām of reason, whose agent is latent, its implied form being هو, referring to man. أمامه is an adverb of place borrowed for time, i.e. so that he may continue in his wickedness and persist in it in the times before him and the time that faces him, not desisting from it nor disowning it. The lām of reason is attached to يريد. Al-Jalāl and others parsed it another way, the gist of which is that the lām is redundant (zāʾida) and يفجر is accusative by an implied أن, the maṣdar formed from it and أن being the object of يريد. There is no call for making the lām redundant, so the first view is the correct one.
(يَسْئَلُ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الْقِيامَةِ): the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. he wants to continue in his wickedness while asking, by way of mockery, "when is the Day of Resurrection?". It has also been said to be resumptive. Abū al-Baqāʾ said it is an explanation of ليفجر, so it is explicative and resumptive, or a substitute for the clause before it, since explanation may be by resumption or by substitution. أيان is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to an omitted element in the position of nominative as a fronted khabar, and يوم القيامة is a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(فَإِذا بَرِقَ الْبَصَرُ): the fāʾ is resumptive; إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time attached to the apodosis, which is يقول; the clause برق البصر is a verbal clause in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it.
(وَخَسَفَ الْقَمَرُ): conjoined to برق البصر; it is a past verb and its agent.
(وَجُمِعَ الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ): also conjoined, falling within the scope of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). Their being brought together is one of the greatest signs of Allah.
(يَقُولُ الْإِنْسانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَيْنَ الْمَفَرُّ): the clause يقول الإنسان has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. يوم is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to يقول, and the tanwīn compensates for a clause, i.e. "on the day when the sight is dazzled, etc.". أين is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, the adverb being attached to an omitted element in the position of nominative as a fronted khabar, and المفر is a postponed mubtadaʾ. المفر is a mīmī maṣdar meaning "fleeing", or a noun of place for fleeing; the first has fatḥa on the fāʾ and the second kasra, and it has been read both ways.
(كَلَّا لا وَزَرَ): كلا is a particle of deterrence and rebuke against seeking flight; لا is the lā of generic negation; وزر is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and its khabar is omitted, i.e. "existing, available to them".
(إِلى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمُسْتَقَرُّ):
إلى ربك is a fronted khabar; يومئذ is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to an implied verb indicated by المستقر, i.e. "the matter settles with your Lord on the day when these mentioned things happen". It may not be attached to المستقر, because if it is a maṣdar, [it cannot govern] because [the adverb] precedes it, and if it is a noun of place, it has no governing power at all. المستقر is a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(يُنَبَّؤُا الْإِنْسانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِما قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ):
The clause is explicative and resumptive, as stated before. ينبأ is a passive imperfect verb; الإنسان is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); يومئذ is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to ينبأ; بما is in the position of the second object; the clause قدم together with أخر conjoined to it has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. That is: man will be informed, on the day when these three things happen — the dazzling of sight, the eclipsing of the moon and the bringing together of the sun and the moon — of what he put forward, of deeds he did, and of what he held back, of deeds he did not do.
(بَلِ الْإِنْسانُ عَلى نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ):
بل is a conjunction and transitional digression; الإنسان is a mubtadaʾ; على نفسه is attached to بصيرة. As for بصيرة, it may be the khabar of الإنسان, which is the preferable view, the meaning being: rather man is a clear witness (بصيرة) against himself.
On this view the following question arises: why was the khabar made feminine? The grammarians differed in answering. Some said the hāʾ in it is not for the feminine but for intensiveness. Al-Akhfash said: it is like your saying "so-and-so is a lesson (عبرة) and a proof (حجة)". It has also been said that what is meant by man is his limbs, as though He said: rather his limbs are بصيرة, i.e. witnessing. بصيرة may also be a postponed mubtadaʾ with على نفسه a fronted khabar, the clause being a khabar about الإنسان; on this view بصيرة is an adjective of something omitted, i.e. "a seeing eye" or "limbs", and the tāʾ on this view is for the feminine. Al-Zamakhsharī took this view and said: «بصيرة: a clear proof, described with seeing figuratively, as the signs were described with seeing in His saying: فلما جاءتهم آياتنا مبصرة; or for seeing eyes». It may also be that على نفسه is the khabar and بصيرة an agent of it, the norm for predicates being the singular. The three views are equal in strength and preferability.
(وَلَوْ أَلْقى مَعاذِيرَهُ):
The wāw is circumstantial, [introducing a ḥāl] from the agent latent in بصيرة. لو is conditional; ألقى is a past verb, which is the protasis, whose agent is latent, its implied form being هو; معاذيره is a direct object. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "they would not be accepted, nor received". المعاذير is the plural of معذرة, irregularly, like ملاقيح and مذاكير, plurals of لقحة and ذكر. The grammarians have two views on this and its like: first, that it is the plural of the uttered word, i.e. لقحة; second, that it is the plural of an unuttered, implied word, i.e. ملقحة and مذكار. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: is not the regular plural of معذرة معاذر, [not] معاذير? I say: المعاذير is not a plural of معذرة but a collective noun of it; similar is المناكير for المنكر». Abū Ḥayyān said in comment: «This form is not one of the forms of collective nouns; it is one of the forms of the broken plural, so it is like مذاكير and ملاميح, the singulars of which are لمحة and ذكر, and no one has held that they are collective nouns. It has been said that they are irregular plurals of لمحة and ذكر, or that they are plurals of an unuttered singular, namely مذكار and ملمحة».
(لا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ إِنَّ عَلَيْنا جَمْعَهُ وَقُرْآنَهُ):
The clause is the object of an omitted, resumptive saying. لا is prohibitive; تحرك is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; به is attached to تحرك; لسانك is a direct object. The lām is the lām of reason; تعجل is an imperfect verb, accusative by أن concealed after the lām of reason, and the lām and what lies within its scope are attached to تحرك; به is attached to تعجل. The pronoun is for the Qur'an, i.e. reciting and memorizing it in haste lest it escape you. Then He gave the reason for the prohibition of haste by His saying: إن علينا جمعه. إنّ, its fronted khabar and its postponed noun; قرآنه is conjoined to جمعه.
(فَإِذا قَرَأْناهُ فَاتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ):
The fāʾ is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb for future time, and its clause قرأناه is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. The fāʾ links the apodosis of إذا; اتبع is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being أنت, and قرآنه is a direct object, i.e. be following behind in it and do not keep pace with it [Translator's note: i.e. do not recite along with the angel], and set your mind at rest that it will not remain unpreserved.
(ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنا بَيانَهُ): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; إنّ is a particle resembling the verb; علينا is the fronted khabar of إنّ and بيانه the postponed noun of إنّ.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «لا أقسم بيوم القيامة ولا أقسم بالنفس اللوّامة» there is the device of «ṣiḥḥat al-aqsām» (soundness of the oaths), which the author of al-Mathal al-Sāʾir called «correspondence between meanings». Many examples of it have passed in this book, and we have spoken about it at length. The verse before us is counted among the beauties of division, because of the correspondence of the two things sworn by: He swore first by the Day of Resurrection and then swore by the souls that will be requited on it, upon the reality of resurrection and requital. Glory be to the One who spoke this speech.

dervis-irab:20-40.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ناضِرَةٌ): from النضرة: beautiful and radiant. النضرة is living in comfort, and from it غصن ناضر (a fresh branch). One says نضر ينضر of the class of دخل, نضر ينضر of the class of تعب, and نضر ينضر of the class of ظرف, نضرا, نضرة, نضرا, نضورا and نضارة: the face, the colour, the tree or other things became soft and fine and beautiful, so it is ناضر, نضر and نضير. And أنضر is said of the stick (العود) too. Al-Kumayt said:
ورت بك عيدان المكارم كلها ... وأورق عودي في ثراك وأنضرا
(Through you all the fire-sticks of noble deeds have kindled, and my branch has leafed and grown fresh in your soil.)
In al-Asās: «She has a bracelet of نضر and نضار, which is gold; it has been said that every pure thing, of gold or other, is نضار. And a cup of نضار, which is a tamarisk of wars-yellow [Translator's note: ورسيّ, saffron-like] colour in the lowland of the Ḥijāz. Among the figurative uses: نضر وجهه: his face became beautiful and fresh; a fresh, radiant girl; a fresh boy: radiant. نضّر الله وجهه and أنضره: He made it beautiful; and sometimes نضَره is said without doubling, with وجه منضور, but that is not so good. He said:
نضّر الله أعظما دفنوها ... بسجستان طلحة الطلحات
(May Allah make radiant the bones they buried in Sijistān — Ṭalḥat al-Ṭalaḥāt.)
In the ḥadīth: «May Allah make radiant the one who heard my saying and retained it». نجار نضار: pure stock. Al-Afwah said:
كرم الفعل إذا ما فعلوا ... ونجار في اليمانين نضار
(Noble in deed whenever they act, and of pure stock among the Yemenis.)»
(فاقِرَةٌ): a great calamity that breaks the back, or its vertebrae (فقاره). الفقار is with fatḥa on the fāʾ, as in al-Qāmūs, and it is the plural of فقارة with fatḥa on the fāʾ. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «فقرت الداهية الرجل فقرا, of the class of قتل: the calamity befell him, so he is فقير, فعيل in the sense of مفعول. فقارة الظهر, with fatḥa, is the vertebra, and the plural is فقار with the hāʾ dropped, like سحابة and سحاب. Ibn al-Sikkīt said: one does not say فِقارة with kasra. الفقرة is a dialectal variant of الفقارة, and its plural is فقر and فقرات, like سدرة, سدر and سدرات». In al-Qāmūs: «الفِقر, with kasra, and الفَقرة and الفَقارة, both with fatḥa: what is joined of the bones of the spine from the withers to the coccyx».
(التَّراقِيَ): plural of الترقوة, which is the bone at the top of the chest between the hollow of the throat and the shoulder; there are two collarbones, and the plural is التراقي and الترائق [Translator's note: the source has الترايق]. One says ترقاه ترقاة, i.e. he struck his collarbone; and "his soul has reached the collarbones" when he is near death.
(راقٍ):
An active participle, either from رقى — with fatḥa in the past and kasra in the imperfect — from الرقية, which is speech prepared for seeking a cure, with which the sick person is treated by incantation so that he may be healed; in the ḥadīth: "And what made you know that it is a ruqya?", meaning al-Fātiḥa, and this is one of its names. Or from رقي — with kasra in the past and fatḥa in the imperfect — from الرقي, which is ascending, i.e. the angels say: who will ascend with this soul?
(يَتَمَطَّى): imperfect of تمطّى. There are two views on it. The first is that it is from المطا, which is the back, and its meaning is "to strut", i.e. he stretches his back and twists it in swaggering as he walks. The second is that its origin is يتمطط, from تمطط, i.e. stretched himself; its meaning is that he stretches himself in his walk out of swaggering, and that is a concomitant of swaggering, so it is near to the meaning of the first but differs from it in its root, since the root of المطا is م ط و and the root of the second is م ط ط; the second ṭāʾ was changed to yāʾ only out of dislike for the gathering of like letters. المطيطاء is swaggering and stretching the arms while walking, and المطيط is the thick water at the bottom of the trough, because it stretches out in it. In the ḥadīth: "When my community walks with a swagger (المطيطاء), and Persia and Rome serve them, their might will be set among themselves." In the books of language: among figurative uses is تمطّى الليل when the night grows long. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فقلت له لما تمطى بصلبه ... وأردف إعجازا وناء بكلكل
(I said to it, when it stretched out its back, followed with its hindquarters and rose heavily with its breast.)
And Bayhas said:
كلما قلت قد تقضّى تمطّى ... حالك اللون دامسا يحموما
(Whenever I say it has ended, it stretches out — jet-coloured, pitch-dark, black.)
(سُدىً): neglected, not charged with the laws. One says إبل سدى, i.e. left untended; and أسديت حاجتي, i.e. I let it go to waste. The meaning of أسدى إليه معروفا (he did him a kindness) is that he made it like something lost with the one to whom it was done, not mentioning it nor reminding him of it as a favour. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «السدى, on the measure of الحصى, of a cloth is the opposite of the weft (اللحمة); it is the warp stretched lengthwise in weaving. أسديت الثوب: I set up its warp. السدى is also the dew of the night, by which crops live; سديت الأرض, so it is سدية, of the class of تعب: its dew became abundant. سدا الرجل سدوا, of the class of قال: he stretched his hand towards something; سدا البعير سدوا [Translator's note: the source has «وسدّ البعير»]: he stretched his foreleg in going; أسديته with alif: I left it سدى, i.e. neglected; and أسديت إليه معروفا: I placed a kindness with him».
In al-Lisān, al-Asās and others: «A neglected camel (جمل سدى) and neglected camels; a people left to themselves; land left untilled. And السندي [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently a corruption of الندى] and السدى fell, which is what falls by night. This cloth: its warp is silk. أسديته; the weaver أسدى the cloth and سدّاه. Among figurative uses: "you have set the warp, so put in the weft; you have saddled, so bridle"; أسدى إليه معروفا; سدّى منطقا حسنا (he wove fine speech); and the slanderers سدّوا against him. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
وإنّا لمحقوقون أن لا تردّنا ... أقاويل ما سدّوا علينا ولصّقوا
(We are surely bound not to be turned back by the sayings they wove and pinned upon us.)
أسدى بين القوم: he made peace among them. "You are neither weft nor warp": you neither harm nor benefit. The wind weaves (تسدي) the waymarks and wefts (تنير) them. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
لمن الديار كأنهنّ سطور ... تسدي معالمها الصبا وتنير
(Whose are the dwellings, as though they were lines of writing, whose traces the east wind warps and wefts?)
تسدّاه: he rose over him and seized him from above, as the dew of the night does. He said:
وما أبو سمرة بالرث ألوان ... يوم تسدى الحكم بن مروان
(Abū Samra is not shabby in colours, on the day he came down upon al-Ḥakam ibn Marwān.)
That is, he seized him by his forelock while he was on a horse».
(تَمَنَّى): it is poured into the womb. المني is the gushing fluid that comes out in intercourse.

* I'rab:
(كَلَّا بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ الْعاجِلَةَ): [كلا] is a particle of deterrence and rebuke; بل is a transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī); تحبون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). The address is to the disbelievers of Quraysh and to man in general. It was read with tāʾ, by way of iltifāt (shift of address), and with yāʾ, in the third person. العاجلة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. this world.
(وَتَذَرُونَ الْآخِرَةَ): conjoined to the previous clause; it was also read with tāʾ and yāʾ, as above.
(وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ ناضِرَةٌ إِلى رَبِّها ناظِرَةٌ): وجوه is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ناضرة an adjective of it; يومئذ is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf) by ناضرة; إلى ربها is attached (mutaʿalliq) to ناظرة, and ناظرة is the khabar (predicate) of وجوه. The meaning is that the beautiful faces on the Day of Resurrection are looking at their Lord. This is a sound meaning and an easy analysis. وجوه may also be a mubtadaʾ with ناضرة its khabar, يومئذ being an adverb made accusative by ناضرة; beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted here because the place is a place of detailing. ناظرة then is an adjective of وجوه, or a second khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; إلى ربها is attached to ناظرة. يومئذ is an adverb annexed to its like, and the tanwīn compensates for a clause, i.e. "on the day when the Resurrection takes place". More discussion of these two verses will come in the Benefits section.
(وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ باسِرَةٌ تَظُنُّ أَنْ يُفْعَلَ بِها فاقِرَةٌ): conjoined to what precedes, and the i'rab has been discussed. It must be pointed out that يومئذ does not specify the indefinite noun so as to permit beginning with it, because an adverb of time cannot be an adjective of a concrete thing; it is only governed by باسرة, as we said it is governed by ناضرة above. The clause تظن may be the khabar on the first view, or a khabar after a khabar. أن and what lies within its scope fill the place of the two objects of تظن; بها is attached to يفعل, and فاقرة is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of يفعل. The meaning of ظن here is certainty, or expectation with a predominant conviction, because it is the time when doubts are lifted.
(كَلَّا إِذا بَلَغَتِ التَّراقِيَ): كلا is a deterrent from preferring this world to the Hereafter, and a reminder to them of the death they will come to, at which the transitory world is cut off and one passes from it to the deferred one. إذا is an adverb for future time; the clause بلغت is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. The agent of بلغت is latent (mustatir), its implied form being هي, referring to the soul, which the context of the speech indicates even though it has not been mentioned, as Ḥātim said:
أماويّ ما يغني الثراء عن الفتى ... إذا حشرجت يوما وضاق بها الصدر
(O Māwiyya, of what use is wealth to a young man when one day it rattles in the throat and the breast grows tight with it?)
The Arabs say أرسلت ("it sent down"), meaning "the rain came", and you hardly ever hear them mention the sky. التراقي is a direct object.
(وَقِيلَ مَنْ راقٍ):
The wāw is a conjunction; قيل is a passive past verb, and its deputy agent is latent, its implied form being هو, i.e. those around him [Translator's note: so in the source]. من is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and راق is its khabar; it is nominative, the sign of its nominative being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ that was omitted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. The clause من راق is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). I do not know the meaning of al-Samīn's statement: «This clause is the one standing in place of the agent».
(وَظَنَّ أَنَّهُ الْفِراقُ): the wāw is a conjunction; ظن is a past verb meaning "he was certain". Certainty was called ظن because as long as a person's soul is in his body he hopes for the continuance of life, out of his intense love of it and attachment to it. أنّ and its noun, and the ẓarf [Translator's note: so in the source; الفراق is in fact the khabar] is its khabar; أنّ and what lies within its scope are in the position of accusative, filling the place of the two objects of ظن.
(وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ بِالسَّاقِ): also conjoined; more on its meaning will come in the Rhetoric section.
(إِلى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمَساقُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element which is a fronted khabar; يومئذ is an adverb attached to المساق, annexed to its like, and the tanwīn compensates for four clauses: the soul has reached the collarbones; it is said, who is a healer; he is certain it is the parting; and the shank is wrapped with the shank. المساق is a postponed mubtadaʾ. The apodosis of إذا, which is what governs it, is indicated by His saying إلى ربك يومئذ المساق, i.e. it will be driven to the judgement and will of its Lord. المساق is مَفعَل from السوق, so it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar).
(فَلا صَدَّقَ وَلا صَلَّى): conjoined to His saying أيحسب الإنسان أن لن نجمع عظامه. لا is negative; صدق is a past verb — this is evidence that the negative لا may enter the past tense — whose agent is latent, its implied form being هو, i.e. man. ولا صلى is conjoined to فلا صدق. It has also been said to be conjoined to the clause يسأل أيان يوم القيامة.
(وَلكِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى): also conjoined. لكن is lightened and inoperative; كذب is a past verb, i.e. man, and تولى is conjoined to it.
(ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلى أَهْلِهِ يَتَمَطَّى): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; the secret of it is finding it far-fetched, because whoever has done such a thing ought to fear the descent of Allah's anger, and so walk fearful and subdued; yet this man walks strutting and haughty, vying with the reaches of the sky in height, though he is of lower worth and baser station. إلى أهله is attached to ذهب, and the clause يتمطى is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) from the agent of ذهب.
(أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى): discussion of the i'rab of this word was given at length in Sūrat al-Qitāl.
(ثُمَّ أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى): conjoined to what precedes; the repetition is for emphasis and increase of the threat. Al-Khansāʾ clung to the fringes of this repetition and said:
هممت بنفسي كل الهموم ... فأولى لنفسي أولى لها
(I resolved upon my own life every resolve — so woe to my soul, woe to it.)
(أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسانُ أَنْ يُتْرَكَ سُدىً): the hamza is for a question of denial; يحسب الإنسان is a verb and its agent; أن and what lies within its scope fill the place of the two objects of يحسب. The deputy agent is latent, its implied form being هو. سدى is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يترك.
(أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَنِيٍّ يُمْنى): the hamza is for a question of affirmation and denial; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [to the past] and jussive; يك is a deficient (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the implied sukūn on the nūn omitted for lightening. The noun of يك is latent, its implied form being هو, i.e. man; نطفة is its khabar; من مني is an adjective; the clause يمنى, in the passive, is an adjective of مني. It was also read with tāʾ.
(ثُمَّ كانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى): conjoined to what precedes. The conjunction is with ثم for delay and length of time, because between the second creation, which is the creation of offspring, and the first creation there is delay and a long span, so it had to be conjoined with ثم. كان and its latent noun, and علقة is its khabar. The two fāʾs are for sequence with immediacy.
(فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثى): also conjoined, with immediacy. جعل is a past verb; منه is in the position of the second object; الزوجين is the first object of جعل; الذكر is a badal (substitute) and الأنثى is conjoined to it.
(أَلَيْسَ ذلِكَ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتى): the hamza is for a question of denial and affirmation; ذلك is the noun of ليس, i.e. the doer [of these things]; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and قادر is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of ليس; على أن يحيي الموتى is attached to قادر.

* Rhetoric:
1- The representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya) in His saying «والتفّت الساق بالساق»: a representational metaphor for the severity of the distress of this world on its last day and the severity of the distress of the Hereafter on its first day, because they are two days that have wrapped around each other and become mixed with distress, as the shank wraps around the shank — as it is said, "war has bared its shank", a metaphor for its severity. It has also been said that their wrapping is from the severity of the illness, because it contracts and extends and lays this one over that. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «His shank wrapped around his shank and twisted over it in the agony (عَلَز) of death», which is the trembling that seizes the sick person.
2- In His saying «والتفّت الساق بالساق إلى ربك يومئذ المساق» there is the incomplete paronomasia (al-tajnīs al-nāqiṣ), also called jinās al-tabdīl. It is that in one of the two words there is a letter not found in the other, while all the letters of the other are found in its sister in their order. It has three divisions: a division in which the addition occurs at the beginning of the word, like the addition of the mīm in المساق; a division in which the addition occurs in the middle of the word, as in His saying, the Exalted: وإنه على ذلك لشهيد وإنه لحب الخير لشديد; and a division in which the addition occurs at the end of the word, as in His saying, the Exalted: ثم كلي من كل الثمرات.

* Benefits:
We will not dwell long on the question of the vision of Allah the Exalted on the Day of Resurrection, for it is a question treated in the principles of religion (uṣūl al-dīn), and the proofs of the two ways, the people of the Sunna and the Muʿtazila, are well known. Since al-Zamakhsharī was of the Muʿtazila, and his doctrine is that fronting the object indicates restriction (ikhtiṣāṣ), he said concerning His saying, the Exalted, «إلى ربها ناظرة»: «It is known that they will look at things beyond enumeration and not falling under number, in a place of gathering where all creatures are assembled; so restricting their looking to Him, were He someone looked at, is impossible. It must therefore be taken in a sense with which the restriction is valid; and what is valid with it is that it be from people's saying: "I am looking to so-and-so (أنا إلى فلان ناظر), what he will do for me", intending the sense of expectation and hope. From it is the poet's saying:
وإذا نظرت إليك من ملك ... والبحر دونك زدتني نعما
(Whenever I looked to you, O king — and the sea is less than you — you increased me in favours.)
I heard a woman of the Sarāt begging in Mecca at midday, when people shut their doors and retire to their resting places, saying: "My little eyes are looking to Allah and to you." The meaning is that they expect favour and honour only from their Lord, as they were in this world, fearing none and hoping in none but Him». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «They — meaning the Muʿtazila — held that the meaning is "looking to the mercy of their Lord", or to His reward or His dominion; so they implied an omitted muḍāf. This is a permissible approach in Arabic, as you say "so-and-so is looking to you in such-and-such", i.e. to your doing».
Ibn al-Munayyir, as is his custom, commented on al-Zamakhsharī and said: «How short his tongue is at this verse! How long he hums and expatiates in denying the vision, splitting hairs [lit. "splitting the cloak"], multiplying words and going deep; yet when this verse opened its mouth, all he did in his silence [Translator's note: so in the source; the wording appears disturbed] was to argue that, had vision been meant, it would not have been restricted by the fronting of the object, because it would then not be restricted on the assumption of the vision of Allah the Exalted. He does not know that the one who enjoys the vision of the beauty of the Face of Allah the Exalted will not turn his glance away from it, nor prefer another to it, nor set any other object of sight beside Him, Mighty and Majestic; and it is fitting that he should restrict his vision to the One like whom there is nothing. We see the lover in this world: when you grant him sight of his beloved, he will not turn from him for a moment nor prefer anything to him — so how about the lover of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, if he were to miss looking at His Noble Face? We ask Allah the Great not to turn His Face away from us, and to protect us from the slippery places of innovation and the stumbles of doubt; He is sufficient for us, and the best Disposer of affairs».
